## Review Verdict

| evidence_id | locator | excerpt check | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| EF-E01d4d5302506 | page 91, char 987-1785 | Excerpt states contribution rate rises to 15% by 2030, employer target 13.875% for high earners, subsidies for low earners; current rates 1.125% employee / 0.225% government / 5.15% employer yielding 6.5%-10% range. Claim matches verbatim. | **Accept** |
| EF-Efcd86c5a6dfc | page 91, char 1785-2938 | Excerpt confirms 2021 reform lowered minimum from ~25 to 15 years, scheduled to rise to 20 years by 2031, applies to both funded pension and minimum pension; 2023 first pensioners. Claim faithful to excerpt. | **Accept** |
| EF-E7b5158df7dbd | page 91, char 2702-3338 | Excerpt states pre-2021 single minimum ~MEX$40,000; from 2021 minimum pension differs by earnings and career length, lowest minimum rose to MEX$45,000 for 20+ years contributions, average wage earner minimum more than doubled to MEX$85,000/year. Claim accurate. | **Accept** |
| EF-E70aaec08eb2f | page 92, char 0-416 | Excerpt: "From 2022, fees cannot exceed average fees in Chile, Colombia, and the U.S." Claim matches. | **Accept** |
| EF-Ebd5fa8983510 | page 92, char 416-980 | Excerpt: government spending on pensions rose from 1.4% of GDP (2000) to 4.0% of GDP (2021). Claim faithful; caveat on adverse labor market effects noted in excerpt. | **Accept** |
| EF-E05fb0b351eab | page 92, char 980-1660 | Excerpt enumerates three adverse channels: early-retirement → possible decline in older-worker LFP; earnings-history linkage → reduced formal-work incentives; employer contribution rise → larger labor wedge pushing to informal sector. Claim faithful. | **Accept** |
| EF-Ebf34d08fcc9d | page 93, char 0-941 | Excerpt states Mexico exports to CA = 1.7% of total exports (2021); imports from CA = 0.6% of total imports. FTA signed 2011, implemented 2013. Claim accurate. | **Accept** |
| EF-E01a771565690 | page 93, char 749-1373 | Excerpt states 5.8% of CA exports to Mexico (2021), 13.5% of CA imports from Mexico; Nicaragua, Guatemala, Belize >8% export exposure; Nicaragua exposure rose post-2013 FTA; Guatemala, El Salvador, Honduras >15% import exposure. Claim faithful. | **Accept** |
| EF-E6e2b9ea76403 | page 94, char 594-1418 | Excerpt supports the listed mechanisms (converging trade rules, regulatory standards, infrastructure, human capital, customs cooperation) and notes NAFTA (1994) is referenced in the broader Annex XIV context. However, the **specific NAFTA (1994) customs-cooperation recommendation** is not explicitly stated in this excerpt window. Escalate: the claim attributes a recommendation to replicate U.S.-Mexico NAFTA customs programs in the Southern border, which the excerpt does not directly contain. The excerpt supports the general "customs cooperation" recommendation but not the specific NAFTA 1994 replication point. | **Escalate** — specific NAFTA replication wording not supported by this excerpt window; excerpt supports only the general customs-cooperation recommendation |
| EF-E88a80426f72e | page 94, char 778-1519 | Excerpt confirms FTA resulted in tariff-line liberalization by Mexico across range of products with commitment to further tariff elimination (citing WTO 2015). Claim matches. | **Accept** |
| EF-Ef3be40fc1979 | page 97, char 0-803 | Excerpt confirms team led by Thomas Helbling; meetings Sep 12-23, 2022 in Mexico City; met Finance Secretary Ramírez de la O, Governor Rodríguez Ceja, Labor Secretary Alcalde, Economy Secretary Clouthier. Fund Relations note dated August 31, 2022. Claim accurate. | **Accept** |
| EF-E865d52700c24 | page 97, char 803-1663 | Excerpt confirms Article VIII sections 2/3/4 acceptance, timely data adequate for surveillance, SDDS subscription, free-floating arrangement. Quota/holdings/reserve position figures and FCL amounts are explicitly tabulated in the excerpt. Claim faithful. | **Accept** |
| EF-Ed94f9103e29d | page 97, char 1428-2118 | Excerpt tabulates all nine FCL arrangements with dates, expirations, and amounts; Nov 19, 2021 FCL = SDR 35,650.80 million, 0.00 drawn, expires Nov 18, 2023; footnote confirms Nov 26, 2018 access reduction. All quantities in claim match the table exactly. | **Accept** |
| EF-E96194b7bb160 | page 98, char 0-175 | Excerpt: zero total 2022; SDR 0.15 million charges/interest each year 2023-2026; no principal. Claim accurate. | **Accept** |
| EF-Ec7d46134cd2b | page 98, char 573-794 | Excerpt: "last Article IV consultation was concluded by the Executive Board on November 3, 2021. The staff report was published as IMF Country Report No. 20/293." Claim matches verbatim. | **Accept** |
| EF-Eaa77eb9d4118 | page 98, char 573-1569 | Excerpt enumerates TA engagements 2013-2021 by department and purpose; 2021 FAD = Public Assets and Liabilities Management; 2017 FAD = Revenue Administration (also 2016). Claim accurate. Note: excerpt also shows 2012 FAD Pension and Health Systems, which is outside the claim's stated 2013-2021 range but does not contradict the claim. | **Accept** |

### Notes
- **EF-E6e2b9ea76403 escalation**: The specific claim that Mexico should "replicat[e] in the Southern border the customs cooperation programs and mechanisms Mexico has with the U.S. under NAFTA (1994)" is **not present in the cited excerpt window** (page 94, char 594-1418). The excerpt supports the general customs-cooperation recommendation but not the NAFTA-1994-specific wording. The reviewer flags this as a locator/claim mismatch: either the excerpt window is incomplete (additional content on page 94 or adjacent pages contains the NAFTA reference), or the claim overstates what the cited source says. Recommend re-extracting a wider window from Annex XIV or relocating the locator before downstream use.
